hypothesis: The core's CMD25 descriptor-DMA write passes a strict controller model that accepts only the registers the vendor sequence uses.
narrative:
Core-level checks, all passing in checks/sunxi-mmc-write.py (driver checks/sunxi-mmc-write-dma.c). The model accepts only the registers the sequence uses, checks the command word, block size and count, A12A, argument, the threshold word, FTRGL, the descriptor chain and the cache phases, consumes the descriptors one per poll, and raises the interrupts and DAT0 busy on a schedule. Mutations of the threshold enable, the automatic stop, the first descriptor flag, the programming wait and the PIO-only data check each fail the check.
Checks required before any board run, all in place: the strict controller model refuses any register access the sequence does not use, models the IDMAC consuming descriptors in order, OWN clearing, the data-end and automatic-stop interrupts, and DAT0 busy that outlasts the data. The real core is driven through 1, 2, 255 and 256 blocks, a DAT0 busy of several polls, a data CRC error, a card error in the CMD25 or CMD12 response, and a timeout; each ends in the terminal state the CMD24 path ends in. checks/sd-read-only.py passes with CMD24 and CMD25 absent from the read-only set, and --elf passes on the linked large-region image. A boundary check proves no byte outside the requested range is written (the model compares the whole card).
Register filter for the bounded writer: checks/a733-mmc-native-filter.py runs the real filter on the host (the AArch64 task test and the register accesses sit behind hooks under A733_MMC_NATIVE_HOST_TEST). It changes each of the 32 bits of the exact CMD25 word in turn and requires every changed word to be refused, adds the clock-update form directly, and covers block size and count, range edges and straddles, the unbound, unverified, closed, eMMC and foreign-task states, byte-addressed and unidentified cards at the binding, and a read-only build that refuses CMD25 and the threshold write even when a verified object is forced into it. The hole it closed: the adapter's command filter skipped its index switch for any word with the clock-update bit set (a clock update is not a card command), so a word with index 25, the write bit and the clock-update bit reached the controller without the bounded rule; every word with index 25 now passes the rule first, and the exact word excludes the clock-update bit. The check fails if the first-version behaviour is restored.
Platform gap: the strict CMD25 model drove the core with its own callbacks and never ran the platform's descriptor-chain check (dma_chain in drivers/storage/a733_mmc_platform.c), which refused every write-direction command; see storage-host-coverage-gap in storage.jsonl.
